newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Ghana looks to gas to power booming gold sector.
newsitem.headline: Ghana looks to gas to power booming gold sector.

text.p: Ghana is adopting innovative ways to tap into its undeveloped gas reserves to provide secure electricity supplies for its booming gold mining sector, delegates attending the African Upstream conference heard on Friday.

Ghana National Petroleum Corp (GNPC) chief executive Tsatu Tsikata said Ghana also supported plans to build a West African gas pipeline project to pool gas in the region and support industrial and other development.
He said GNPC was focusing on the offshore Tano Basin in the west of the country, where a number of new gold mines had opened recently.
The new investors include South African giants such as Gold Fields of South Africa and Gencor Ltd.

Tsikata said that until now Ghana had relied mainly on hydroelectrical power, but a random cycle of dry and wet periods had caused "a high level of uncertainty of power output" which had affected industry.

The Tano Basin straddles the border between Ghana and Ivory Coast, and Tsikata said an agreement in principle had been reached between GNPC, Houston-based independent United Meridian Corp and Ivory Coast oil company Petoci to pool resources to develop the fields.

A 28-km pipeline across the border would tie Ivory Coast's reserves into barge-mounted turbines built by Westinghouse Electric Corp that will be placed in the coastal lagoon directly ashore the Tano fields.

"The key will be this central platform gathering concept as this will enable us to look at other potential around the Tano fields and move further east" to fields that had not yet been appraised, Tsikata said.
"This will be a pioneering example of cross-border oil and gas infrastructure (development) in this part of the world."
The barge turbines are expected to initially produce 130 MW of power per cycle and are scheduled to be brought onstream by mid-1997.
"We will then be able to secure power supplies for the new mining companies that are coming in," Tsikata said.
The generation and transmission of power will be controlled by Western Power Company, a private company to be listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange.

Tsikata said U.S. Eximbank had approved cover of $253 million for the project and direct loans of $62 million would also be made available. Further funding was being sought from other U.S. agencies, Japan and France.
GNPC was also involved in a project to study the possibility of bringing Nigeria's large gas reserves into a regional pipeline that also pooled smaller deposits in neighouring countries.

"Nigeria is burning nearly a trillion cubic feet of gas a day and if those gas reserves, instead of being burnt, could be made available to a regional pipeline," the region as a whole would benefit, Tsikata said.
